I work in electronics sourcing from China — finding manufacturers, buying components, and following orders through to shipment. On boards specifically: single and double-sided, multilayer and higher-density work, and full turnkey assembly — bare PCB from one shop, components from authorised distributors, SMT and test at another, then packaging and export paperwork. I don't design boards; I make sure the board you specified is built correctly, on time, at the price quoted.

In practice that means:

Shortlisting factories in Shenzhen, Dongguan, Suzhou and Kunshan on capability, process limits, MOQ and lead time — not price alone.

Verifying components before anything is committed: authorised channel or broker, date codes, distributor invoices.

Attending first article and pilot builds, checking workmanship against IPC-A-610, and chasing non-conformities until they close.

Coordinating test, packaging and export documents, with photo or video evidence at each handover.

Working in English and Mandarin throughout, so the spec doesn't drift between you and the factory.

Send me your board types and volumes, and I'll come back with a factory shortlist and indicative pricing as a first step.

• Source electronic parts and components  
• Manage supplier communication and quality checks  

The agent should already have hands-on experience with:  
• Simple single- or double-layer PCB boards  
• Multi-layer or high-density PCB boards  
• Full PCBA assembly with parts, testing, and packaging  
• Sourcing agent experience

What I expect from you:  
1. Create and post an attractive job listing in  English.  
2. Actively search local talent pools (job boards, WeChat groups, industry events, referrals).  
3. Screen résumés, conduct first-round interviews, and verify references.  
4. Present a short-list (at least three qualified candidates) with interview summaries and your hiring recommendation.  

Fluency in Chinese hiring practices and familiarity with electronics supply chains are essential for success. I’ll provide final interview questions and make the last selection; you manage everything up to that point.  

Please outline your approach, the platforms you’ll tap, and a realistic timeline for delivering the short-list.
